draft.title: Evidence for evolution
card: Fossils
Fossils are preserved remains or traces of past life. Deeper rock layers are usually older, so fossils in layers show how living things changed over time.
Bone structure
Some animals have similar bone patterns in limbs that do different jobs, such as a human arm, a bat wing and a whale flipper. This points to a shared ancestor.
DNA
DNA is the code that carries an organism's instructions. Species with more similar DNA are usually more closely related, and share a more recent ancestor.
Together
Fossils, similar bone structures and shared DNA together show that species have changed over time and share common ancestors.
draft.remember: Fossils, bone structures and DNA all point to shared ancestors.

a.q: Two species are found to have DNA that is very similar. What does this most suggest about them?
opts: They share a fairly recent common ancestor
They live in the same habitat today
They have exactly the same bone structures
One species evolved from the other directly
a.why: More similar DNA usually means a more recent shared ancestor. It does not show that one species came from the other, because both can descend from a common ancestor.
a.clue: Think about how closely related species share ancestors.

b.q: A deep rock layer holds a simple fossil, and a higher layer holds a more complex relative. What does this best show?
opts: Living things in this group changed over time
Both organisms lived at exactly the same time
The higher fossil must have evolved from the lower one
The deeper rock layer formed after the higher one
b.why: Deeper layers are usually older, so the fossils show a change in the group over time. The fossils alone do not prove that the higher one descended directly from the lower one.
b.clue: Which layer is usually older, and what does a change between layers show?

proposal.title: Evidence for evolution
card: Fossils
Fossils are preserved remains or traces of past life. Deeper rock layers are usually older, so fossils in layers show how living things changed over time.
Bone structure
Some animals have similar bone patterns in limbs that do different jobs, such as a human arm, a bat wing and a whale flipper. This points to a shared ancestor.
DNA
DNA is the code that carries an organism's instructions. Species with more similar DNA are usually more closely related, and share a more recent ancestor.
Together
These three kinds of evidence come from different sources, yet they agree: species have changed over time and share common ancestors.
proposal.remember: Fossils, bone structures and DNA all point to shared ancestors.

a.q: Two species are found to have DNA that is very similar. What does this most suggest about them?
opts: They share a recent common ancestor
They share a distant common ancestor
They live in similar habitats today
They eat similar kinds of food today
a.why: More similar DNA usually means species are more closely related, so they share a more recent ancestor. A distant common ancestor fits species whose DNA is less alike. DNA shows how related species are, not where they live or what they eat.
a.clue: Does similar DNA tell you about relatedness or about lifestyle?

b.q: A deep rock layer holds a simple fossil, and a higher layer holds a more complex relative. What does this best show?
opts: Living things in this group changed over time
Both organisms lived at the same point in time
The deeper rock layer formed after the higher one
Living things in this group stayed the same
b.why: Deeper layers are usually older, so the simple fossil comes from an earlier time than the complex one. That shows the group changed over time. The deeper layer forming later reverses the usual order of rock layers.
b.clue: Which rock layer is usually older?
